> A web UI for your instances with `cwcli ui`, a verified backup store with `cwcli backups`, scheduled jobs, sign-in integrations, and a much safer `apps update <project> frappe`.

### Breaking Changes

* `cwcli apps update <project> frappe` now resets only the frappe app to its remote branch and migrates each site under its own maintenance mode, instead of running bench's bench-wide `bench update --reset`, which hard-reset every app on the bench. It also refuses, and exits 1 with nothing changed, while frappe holds uncommitted changes or commits that exist on no remote; pass `--force` to accept that loss.
* `cwcli rm`, `rm-site` and `rm-bench` now move their verified backups into the backup store (`~/.cwcli/backups/`) as `before-removal` sets instead of leaving them in the instance's archive directory, so they outlive the instance.

### New Features

* `cwcli ui` opens a local web UI (bound to `127.0.0.1`, shipped prebuilt inside the package) over every instance, bench, site and app: live process health, searchable logs, the `doctor` health check, a command palette, and the matching `cwcli` command beside each action.
* In the web UI, lifecycle actions and long verbs (`init`, app install, update and checkout, backup, migrate, run-tests, build, new site, new bench) run as detached jobs that keep going when the tab closes, with Interrupt, a Retry button for failed jobs, and a typed confirmation of the exact name before anything destructive runs.
* The web UI has an apps catalog of the Frappe apps on your GitHub, GitLab.com and self-hosted GitLab accounts, showing where each one is installed and offering to install it.
* The web UI signs in with an administrator account (`admin` / `admin`, changed on first sign-in) and has Admin, Operator and Viewer roles; `cwcli admin reset-password` recovers the account from the host.
* Settings > Integrations in the web UI adds LDAP / Active Directory sign-in and a machine-wide S3 backup target, each turned on only after its connection test passes.
* `cwcli integrations add <repository-url>` (or the web UI) installs a community integration for sign-in or the backup target from a GitHub or GitLab repository, after showing you the exact commit to review.
* The web UI has animated gradient themes and an Appearance setting for the theme, light, dark or system colours, and turning the motion off.
* `cwcli backups` keeps verified backup sets outside every instance: capture, verify, restore into any site, bench or instance, clone or move sites, sendme transfers, restore drills, retention with a dry-run prune, a daily schedule, and encrypted S3 off-site copies.
* `cwcli schedule` runs backups, updates, migrate, restarts and other jobs on a timetable, with guards for maintenance windows, quiet hours, stopped instances and free disk; removals can never be scheduled.
* `cwcli new-site`, `cwcli new-bench` and `cwcli dev-mode` add a site to a bench, add a bench to an instance, and turn developer mode on or off.
* `cwcli db-access check|repair` finds and fixes site database users tied to an old container address, and `start`, `restart` and the core update now name a refused database login instead of showing a bare 500.
* `cwcli apps update <project> frappe` runs a preflight that catches, in seconds and with nothing changed, the problems that used to fail late: a branch missing on the remote, a dead remote, a held migrate lock, new code that needs a newer Python or Node, a Frappe major upgrade, or an app whose frappe-dependencies do not fit. `--no-preflight` skips it, and `--fix-branches` switches a mismatched app to the matching `version-N` branch.
* `cwcli status` reports bench-wide maintenance mode and a paused scheduler, and names the command that clears them.

### Bug Fixes

* `rm-site` and `rm-bench` now take the same verified backup as `cwcli rm` before dropping a site, and a failed backup drops nothing; before, bench could drop the database even when its own backup failed.
* `cwcli init` now gives MariaDB the database root password you set, instead of only passing it to `bench new-site` and failing with MySQL error 1045; failed steps name the plain cause, such as a rejected password or a full disk.
* Re-running `cwcli init` against a stopped instance starts its containers as they are, instead of pulling a newer image and breaking the bench's Python environment.
* `cwcli start` recreates an instance's compose network when a WSL or Docker crash removed it.
* `restore --latest` now finds backups of sites with hyphens in their names.
* `cwcli axi run-tests` reports a failing Frappe v14/v15 test run as failed.
* Image pulls that fail in Docker's credential helper are retried, and a missing helper is named.
* Turning on start-at-boot for auto-inspect or the credential bridge no longer stops the running daemon, and both daemons start as fresh processes that no longer hold the calling command's locks.
* `cwcli doctor` checks `gh`/`glab` sign-in for each credential-bridge host.
* The credential bridge explains how to fix an instance workspace it cannot write to, instead of failing with a bare permission error.
* Read-only commands such as `cwcli --version` no longer create the cache directory.
